DECISION 
 
1. 
The appeal is allowed. 
 
2. 
The Tribunal confirms a band E entry with effect from 19 May 2025 on the subject property. 
 
STATEMENT OF REASONS 
 
Introduction 
 
3. 
The appellant served a proposal against the subject property’s band F entry in the valuation 
list. The appellant’s proposal was made on 8 February 2026 which was within six months of 
him becoming the council taxpayer in respect of the subject property. The appellant sought a 
reduction to band E. The listing officer (LO) determined that the proposal was not well 
founded and issued a decision notice to that effect on 27 February 2026. The appellant made 
an appeal to this Tribunal against that decision notice on 6 March 2026. 
 
4. 
The LO reviewed the appeal and proposed a reduction in the property’s council tax band 
from band F to band E with effect from 19 May 2025. The appellant accepted the proposal 
and both parties signed a form of agreement. The signed agreement was subsequently 
placed before the panel for confirmation of the band alteration. 
 
5. 
This statement of reasons is not and does not purport to be a full verbatim record of 
proceedings. 
 
Conclusion 
 
6. 
As the parties were both in agreement that the band should be reduced to band E, the panel 
make the following order. 
 
Order  
 
7. 
Under the provisions of Regulation 38 (2) and (9) of The Valuation Tribunal for England 
(Council Tax and Rating Appeals) (Procedure) Regulations 2009, the VTE orders the Listing 
Officer to alter the Valuation List within two weeks of the date of this order to show band E for 
the subject property with effect from 19 May 2025. 
 
8. 
Under Regulation 38(9), the Listing Officer must comply with this order within two weeks of 
the date of its making    
 
 
Right of further appeal 
 
9. 
Any party who is aggrieved at the Tribunal’s decision has a statutory right of further appeal to 
the High Court on a point of law pursuant to Regulation 43 of the Tribunal Procedure 
Regulations. A party does not require permission to appeal from the Tribunal. Any appeal 
must be made directly to the High Court using Form N161 (Appellant’s Notice) within four 
weeks of the date this decision and statement of reasons was issued. 
 
10. Further information regarding this statutory right of further appeal, and the parties’ other 
rights, is contained in the guidance booklet “A guide to tribunal decisions” available on the 
Tribunal’s website at www.valuationtribunal.gov.uk/guidance-booklets/.
